hints.title: Large-Scale Greedy Choice
hints.text: The multiplier effect holds regardless of dimensions up to one hundred thousand. Greedy choice on greatest costs prevents ballooning totals.

hints.title: 64-bit Integer Accumulation
hints.text: Because dimensions and cut costs can reach one hundred thousand, intermediate products exceed 32-bit limits and require 64-bit accumulation.

hints.title: Merge-Step Mechanics
hints.text: Maintain descending sorted pointers. At each step consume the higher cost cut and multiply by current perpendicular piece count.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minimumCost(self, m: int, n: int, horizontalCut: list[int], verticalCut: list[int]) -> int:
        horizontalCut.sort(reverse=True)
        verticalCut.sort(reverse=True)
        h, v = 0, 0
        h_pieces, v_pieces = 1, 1
        total_cost = 0
        while h < len(horizontalCut) and v < len(verticalCut):
            if horizontalCut[h] >= verticalCut[v]:
                total_cost += horizontalCut[h] * v_pieces
                h_pieces += 1
                h += 1
            else:
                total_cost += verticalCut[v] * h_pieces
                v_pieces += 1
                v += 1
        while h < len(horizontalCut):
            total_cost += horizontalCut[h] * v_pieces
            h += 1
        while v < len(verticalCut):
            total_cost += verticalCut[v] * h_pieces
            v += 1
        return total_cost
```

complexity.time: O(m log m + n log n)
complexity.notes: Fast sorting followed by a single linear two-pointer pass.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute-force explores permutations yielding factorial explosions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) extra space beyond sorted arrays.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handles 64-bit integer overflow and explains greedy exchange argument.
